provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The rule already works the same way under every rotation and reflection, so the emitted program uses visible coordinates with no axis specialization. Only the colour roles are specialized: the outline colour is palette[1] and the fill/ray colour is palette[2]. The background is the most common colour other than the outline colour. Each 4-connected component of outline colour is one 4x4 box. The generator's notches are never corners, so the bounding box is always the full square. The program fills the box interior with the fill colour. It then finds the border cell that is background (the gap). The side that cell lies on sets the outward direction in visible coordinates: top row goes up, bottom row goes down, left column goes left, right column goes right. Reflected or rotated scenes are therefore handled naturally. The ray paints every background cell from the gap to the grid edge. Unlike the archived solver, it does not stop at non-background cells; it skips them. This matches the generator in one rare case: an earlier box's ray passes through a later box's area. There the later box's outline overwrites the ray but the ray continues beyond it. In all other valid scenes the generator rejects collisions, so this is equivalent to the archived behaviour. The approved fixtures are consistent with this uniform rule.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the input is a valid generator scene: non-overlapping 4x4 outlines in palette[1], each with exactly one non-corner gap, and a background that is the most common non-outline colour. Malformed inputs fall back to similar behaviour, but no particular result is guaranteed: a component with no gap gets only its interior filled, and multiple gaps each emit a ray. No tests were run.
